Independent replay constructed T_n using pair-intersection tests, enumerated compatible k-edge subsets, indexed sorted edge lists, and applied every one-edge replacement. For n=3 through 8 the counts were 3,12,30,90,630,2520; jump degrees 2,11,29,4,22,58 and slide degrees 2,6,10,4,12,20. Both graphs had ten size-9 components at n=6 and one in each other tested case.
correctness.rationale: An edge of T_n specifies two intersecting ground pairs, hence a unique triple and center. Two selected edges are compatible if and only if their ground supports are disjoint, so maximum size is floor(n/3) and dividing by the free-label, block and leaf permutations gives n!/(r!2^k k!). After deletion the replacement is confined to the r+3 available labels. The jump degree counts all possible marked triples there except the old one; the slide degree counts edges incident to the two endpoints of the old edge in T_{r+3} other than itself. These are disjoint alternatives, since distinct edges share at most one endpoint, and distinct deleted edges cannot yield the same neighbor. For r=0 the invariant support partition gives independent K3 center changes. For r>0 a center change followed by a slide exchanges any designated occupied label with any free label. Such transpositions generate all placements (a third slot provides a buffer for same-class transpositions), and centers can be set afterward. This also works for k=1, including n=3 where there is just one component.
residual_risks: Replay was bounded to 3≤n≤8 and checked component sizes, not Cartesian-product isomorphism; that is proved by the support invariant and independent center changes.

value.rationale: The two natural models have the same reachable components but very different local mobility: e.g., with two free labels there are 29k jump choices but only 10k slide choices. The exact, labeled all-order comparison clarifies why allowing a whole matching edge to jump does not change reachability in this family despite adding many transitions. This is distinct utility from recomputing the known residue transition alone.
residual_risks: Limited to maximum matchings and single-edge moves on this family; no diameter, mixing, or broader reconfiguration bound is shown.
